questions.question: Is failure to develop full engine power a reason to check the air-intake/exhaust system, and does a 0.20-inch dust-unloader center opening exceed the preventive maintenance standard?
If an engine fails to develop full power and the dust-unloader center opening measures 0.20 inch, should the air-intake/exhaust system be checked, and is the unit fully mission capable?
Is failure to develop full engine power a reason to check the air-intake/exhaust system, and does a dust-unloader center opening of 0.20 inch make the unit not fully mission capable?

claims.text: Failure to develop full engine power is a stated reason to check the air-intake/exhaust system.
A dust-unloader center opening of 0.20 inch (5.08 mm) exceeds the preventive maintenance check standard of 1/8 inch (3.175 mm).
A dust-unloader center opening of 0.20 inch (5.08 mm) makes the unit not fully mission capable.
